chat.why: Composite of every BenchLM category: its knowledge and reasoning inputs resemble chat questions, but most weight is agentic, coding and multimodal, and BenchLM has no questions of its own.

math_code.why: Includes the math and coding category inputs (competition math, repo-level SWE, LiveCodeBench) diluted by everything else; no questions of its own.

agentic.why: Agentic inputs (Terminal-Bench, OSWorld, BrowseComp, tau2/tau3, BFCL v4) are one slice of a much wider mix; no questions of its own.

3.1.overlap: Composite only: its inputs include HLE, MMLU-Pro and BFCL v4 (weighted) and SimpleQA and MATH-500 (display only) -- the benchmarks behind Yugos hle, mmlu_pro, bfcl, simpleqa_verified and math. BenchLM itself holds no questions.
3.1.summary: BenchLM's overall score is a weighted aggregate of other benchmarks' published model scores (all categories); it has no questions, answers or per-question results, so it cannot be used as question data -- only as model-level prior scores or a pointer to its constituent benchmarks.

chat.why: different skill: multi-step agent tasks, not single-answer chat questions

math_code.why: Mostly agent tasks; only terminal/agentic-coding parts touch code, and in a long multi-step setting.

agentic.why: Composite of multi-step agent benchmarks (Terminal-Bench, BrowseComp, OSWorld, MCP Atlas, tau2/tau3-bench, BFCL v4, VendingBench...): the skill is related to the hidden agentic part, but many need screenshots, browsing or very long horizons, and BenchLM has no questions of its own.

3.2.overlap: Includes BFCL v4 (2% weight) and BFCL v3 (display only), the family of the live Yugos bfcl set.
3.2.summary: Weighted aggregate of ~45 published agent benchmark scores (terminal, browser research, computer use, tool use). No questions of its own; useful only as model-level agentic priors and as a list of candidate agent datasets (tau2/tau3, MCP Atlas, BFCL v4) to fetch directly.

chat.why: different skill: software engineering and code generation

math_code.why: Mostly repo-level agentic SWE tasks (SWE-bench Pro, DeepSWE, FrontierSWE, NL2Repo) plus some function-level code (LiveCodeBench v6/Pro, SciCode); Yugos code is single-prompt Python library functions; BenchLM has no questions of its own.

agentic.why: Agentic coding in a terminal harness is tool use, but not function-calling from schemas or customer-service style tasks.

3.3.summary: Weighted aggregate of ~35 coding benchmark scores, dominated by repo-level software-engineering agents; BigCodeBench and DS-1000 are not among its inputs. No questions of its own; only model-level coding priors.

chat.why: Puzzle-style inputs (LisanBench, chess and mystery-game puzzles, NYT Connections, LiveBench reasoning, ARC-AGI-2) resemble bbeh reasoning puzzles, but long-context inputs (LongBench v2, MRCR v2, Graphwalks 128K-1M) and interactive game arenas do not; no questions of its own.

math_code.why: Logic/data-analysis reasoning, not math problems or code.

agentic.why: different skill: game arenas are interactive but give no tool schemas

3.4.summary: Weighted aggregate of ~22 reasoning benchmark scores (puzzles, games, long-context retrieval). BBH appears display-only (bbeh's predecessor, different questions); BBEH itself is not an input. No questions of its own; only model-level reasoning priors.

chat.why: different skill: needs images, documents, video or audio (MMMU-Pro, OCRBench, Video-MME, CharXiv, VoxPopuli); Yugos is text-only

math_code.why: different skill: visual math (MathVision, DynaMath) needs images

agentic.why: different skill: GUI grounding / visual tasks need screenshots

3.5.summary: Weighted aggregate of vision, document, video and audio benchmark scores; almost every input needs a non-text input, so it cannot stand in for Yugos's text-only questions. No questions of its own.

chat.why: Knowledge QA mix (GPQA-D, SuperGPQA, MMLU-Pro, HLE, SimpleQA, MedXpertQA text, HealthBench) matches chat's knowledge parts; HealthBench is multi-turn and rubric-judged; several inputs are live Yugos sets; no questions of its own.

math_code.why: Expert knowledge recall, with only HLE's math share overlapping math problems.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls

3.6.overlap: Includes HLE, HLE w/o tools and HLE-Diamond (Yugos hle), MMLU-Pro (Yugos mmlu_pro) and SimpleQA (display only; superset of Yugos simpleqa_verified).
3.6.summary: Weighted aggregate of knowledge benchmark scores (GPQA-D, MMLU-Pro, HLE, HealthBench, MedXpertQA, SuperGPQA). No questions of its own, but it names the right families; the underlying datasets (several of them live Yugos sets) should be used directly.

chat.why: Non-English knowledge tests (Global-MMLU Lite, MMLU-ProX, INCLUDE, cEval, NOVA-63) while Yugos is English-only; the biggest weight (22%) is SWE Multilingual coding; no questions of its own.

math_code.why: SWE Multilingual is repo-level coding in many programming languages; MGSM Bengali and PolyMath are non-English math.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls

3.7.overlap: MMLU-ProX is MMLU-Pro translated into other languages, i.e. translated copies of the pool behind Yugos mmlu_pro.
3.7.summary: Weighted aggregate of 9 multilingual benchmark scores. Yugos questions are all English, so the fit is weak; no questions of its own.

chat.why: Chat-type skills (constraint following IFBench/LiveBench IF, EQ-Bench, BullshitBench, WritingBench) but graded by constraint checks or judges rather than short reference answers; no questions of its own.

math_code.why: different skill: instruction following and writing

agentic.why: different skill; only the prompt-injection tests (Gray Swan IPI, PromptArmor) involve tool-using agents

3.8.summary: Weighted aggregate of 7 instruction-following / writing / safety benchmark scores. Could hint at how models handle easy everyday chat prompts (the hidden chat part), but has no questions of its own.

chat.why: Competition math; Yugos chat only has math inside hle.

math_code.why: Competition and frontier math with closed-form answers (Apex, IMOAnswerBench, FrontierMath, HMMT, AIME, MATH-500) fits Yugos math/arxivmath, but no code, FrontierMath is private, and BenchLM has no questions of its own.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls

3.9.overlap: MATH-500 (display only) is a 500-problem subset of the MATH test set, the source family of Yugos math; it may share problems with it.
3.9.summary: Weighted aggregate of ~21 math benchmark scores (mostly 2025-2026 competitions plus FrontierMath). No questions of its own; the public constituents (AIME/HMMT 2025-26, MATH-500) are the usable data.

chat.why: Same source as Yugos hle: expert closed-ended questions, 76% exact / 24% MC, LLM judge, median ~126 tokens; 342 of 2,500 need an image (filterable via the image field).

math_code.why: 41% is research-level math with closed-form answers (like arxivmath), judged by LLM rather than Math-Verify; the rest is non-math and there is no code.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls

4.1.overlap: The live Yugos hle set (90 text-only questions) is drawn from this exact dataset (cais/hle, revision pinned by Yugos).
4.1.summary: The full 2,500-question HLE (gated but auto-approved on HF, MIT): the exact pool Yugos samples its hle questions from, so its 2,158 text-only questions are ideal stand-ins for chat:public hle (exclude the 90 live ones). Third-party per-question results exist in LLMRouterBench (HLE 2,158 text-only samples, 13 late-2025 models, LLM judge).

chat.why: This is exactly the pool Yugos hle samples from: text-only expert questions (2,158; 45% math), 76% exact / 24% MC, LLM judge, median ~126 tokens.

math_code.why: 45% is research-level math with closed-form answers (like arxivmath), judged by LLM rather than Math-Verify; no code.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls

4.2.overlap: The live Yugos hle set (90 text-only questions) is drawn from this exact dataset (cais/hle, revision pinned by Yugos).
4.2.summary: The 2,158 HLE questions without an image (count from the Yugos-pinned cais/hle copy): identical in kind to Yugos's hle set and the best stand-in for it once the 90 live questions are excluded. LLMRouterBench lists HLE with 2,158 samples and per-record correctness, tokens and cost for late-2025 models.

chat.why: Fork of HLE in the same format (MC / short answer, same columns) with some easy questions swapped for harder held-out ones; image share not stated.

math_code.why: Same HLE mix with a large math share (exact share not stated); no code.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls

level_guess.why: Dataset card: HLE fork where some easy questions were replaced by harder held-out ones, so at most as easy as full HLE (computed cdf 0.04/0.04/0.28/0.59); shifted slightly harder.

4.3.overlap: Fork of HLE (some questions replaced), so it may share questions with the 90 live Yugos hle questions; not checked.
4.3.summary: Continually updated HLE fork (created 2025-10-07, last modified 2026-09-17; HF metadata lists 1,000 test rows; gated, MIT). Same question style as Yugos hle and slightly harder; no per-model results published anywhere found. HF tags it text-only but it keeps the image column, so the image share is unverified.

chat.why: Cleaned 1,000-question HLE subset in the HLE format (500 reasoning + 500 knowledge, no tools): same kind as Yugos hle; image share not stated.

math_code.why: Expert math is part of the mix (share not stated) with closed-form answers; no code.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls

4.4.overlap: Refined subset of HLE, the source of the live Yugos hle set; ids not checked, so some of the 90 live questions may be in it.
4.4.summary: HLE-Diamond (released 2026-09-22, gated, MIT): 1,000 cleaned HLE questions with a reasoning/knowledge partition column; a less noisy version of the Yugos hle pool. Only aggregate accuracy and token counts are published.

chat.why: The 500 HLE-Diamond 'reasoning' questions: same format and judge as Yugos hle; subject mix not stated.

math_code.why: Reasoning-type expert questions; math share not stated; closed-form answers, no code.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls

4.5.overlap: Refined subset of HLE, the source of the live Yugos hle set; ids not checked, so some of the 90 live questions may be in it.
4.5.summary: Reasoning half of HLE-Diamond, selectable via the partition column of cais/hle-diamond. Good stand-in for the reasoning-heavy part of Yugos hle; only an aggregate bar chart of 10 models is published.

chat.why: The 500 HLE-Diamond 'knowledge' questions: expert-knowledge closed-ended QA in the Yugos hle format.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls

4.6.overlap: Refined subset of HLE, the source of the live Yugos hle set; ids not checked, so some of the 90 live questions may be in it.
4.6.summary: Knowledge half of HLE-Diamond (partition column). Stands in for the knowledge-recall part of Yugos hle, where routing hinges on what a model knows; aggregate results only.

chat.why: Same HLE-Diamond questions, but scored with web search/fetch and a Python sandbox in provider agent CLIs; Yugos chat gives no tools, so scores do not transfer.

math_code.why: Math share solved with a Python sandbox; closed-form answers, no code to write as output.

agentic.why: Multi-step research with generic tools (web_search, web_fetch up to 60k chars, Python) graded on the final answer; not schema function calls or end-state tasks.

4.7.summary: An evaluation setting, not new questions: HLE-Diamond run with web+code tools in Claude Code / Codex CLI / Gemini CLI under a blocklist; only 7 systems' aggregate scores published. Questions are the same as 4.4; the tool-use results mainly show how much tools lift scores.
